videos.script: Quitanda's product pages ask the database for the same few hundred products all day. {{pages}} A cache keeps a copy of those answers in memory. Most requests then never reach the database. Memorystore is that cache, run by Google. Redis, Valkey or Memcached, on machines you size and pay for by the hour. {{products}} There is no emulator for it. So this lesson starts the engine itself on your own computer, the Redis server Ubuntu ships. {{redis}} You will write the usual pattern in Python. Ask the cache first. On a miss, ask the database and keep the answer for five minutes. {{aside}} Then you will break it. A price changes in the database, and the page goes on showing the old one. {{stale}} You will fill the cache to its limit, and send fifty requests at one missing key. {{herd}} And you will stop a primary and promote its replica by hand, which is what the Standard tier does for you. {{failover}}
